passage: Pallavi and her brother Uday had not spoken since the fight about the borrowed bicycle. For two days they passed each other in the courtyard of their house like strangers. Pallavi missed his silly jokes, but her pride sat like a stone in her chest. On the third afternoon Amma roasted peanuts. Pallavi filled half a steel plate and set it beside Uday's homework without a word. "These are for you," she said. Uday looked up. "Sorry I shouted," he said. "Sorry I called you a thief," she said. He pushed the plate to the middle of the table so they could share, and neither of them felt like they had lost anything.

qa.q: What did Pallavi set beside Uday's homework?
qa.a: She set half a steel plate of roasted peanuts beside it.

qa.q: Why did Pallavi not speak first for two days?
qa.a: Her pride sat like a stone in her chest, even though she missed Uday's silly jokes.

qa.q: Why did Pallavi's snack gesture work?
qa.a: It was a small gesture that opened a door without either one having to give in with words, and Uday then said sorry too.

qa.q: How might Uday have felt when the peanuts appeared beside his homework?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and ready to make up, since he looked up and apologised right away.

grounding: After a big fight, a sibling breaks the silence with a small gesture of sharing food and both say sorry.

passage: Wednesday. Sudha walked into class today wearing her yellow hairband, and my heart did a big jump. When Sir asked me to read, I forgot my own name. Then she said, "Can I borrow your ruler?" and I just nodded like a bobblehead. Ugh 😅. I wanted to say something clever. Maybe tomorrow I will say a normal good morning, like I do to everyone. I will not stare at her or follow her around at recess, because that would be weird and not fair to her. It is a funny, warm feeling, and there is nothing wrong with having it. -- Mohit

qa.q: What colour was Sudha's hairband?
qa.a: It was yellow.

qa.q: How was Mohit feeling when Sudha asked to borrow a ruler?
qa.a: Mohit was flustered and shy, able only to nod for lack of words, and Mohit's heart had jumped when she walked in.

qa.q: What is Mohit's plan for handling this shyness respectfully?
qa.a: Mohit plans to say a normal good morning as with everyone, and not to stare at her or follow her at recess.

qa.q: How might Sudha see Mohit's nodding when she asks for the ruler?
qa.a: She probably just sees Mohit lending a ruler, without knowing Mohit's feelings, since Mohit only nodded.

grounding: A child's first crush leaves the child tongue-tied, with a plan to be friendly and give her space.

passage: I'm Sunaina. At the back of my rough notebook, on the last page, I wrote Vikas's name in tiny letters and then covered it with a doodle of a flower. My heart thumped whenever the notebook slid out of my bag. I did not want anyone teasing me. Only my best friend Rani knew, because I had decided she was kind and never repeated things. I told her at the water tank, whispering, and she just squeezed my hand and said, "Your secret is safe." Now, when Vikas laughs in class, I feel a warm tickle inside, and nobody else needs to know about it.

qa.q: Where did Sunaina write Vikas's name?
qa.a: Sunaina wrote it in tiny letters on the last page of the rough notebook.

qa.q: Why did Sunaina cover Vikas's name with a flower doodle?
qa.a: Sunaina did not want anyone to see it and start teasing, so the feeling stayed hidden.

qa.q: How did Sunaina choose who to tell?
qa.a: Sunaina picked a best friend, Rani, because Rani is kind and never repeats things.

qa.q: How might Rani feel about being trusted with the secret?
qa.a: Rani probably felt trusted and caring, since she squeezed Sunaina's hand and promised the secret was safe. 😊

grounding: A child keeps a first crush private and shares it only with one kind friend.

passage: Counsellor's note, by Ishita. Aditi (Class 6) came to my room at lunch, red in the face. Some classmates had been chanting that a boy in her class likes her. She said it felt like everyone was looking at her. I asked what she wanted to say. After a moment she said, "He is kind, but that is not on my mind." We practised a line together: "Thanks for being kind, but that's not on my mind." I reminded her that what he feels belongs to him, and she does not owe anyone a matching one. I have spoken to her class teacher about the chanting, and I will check in with Aditi on Friday.

qa.q: What were the classmates chanting?
qa.a: They were chanting that a boy in her class likes her.

qa.q: How did Aditi feel, and what did she want to say about the boy?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed and watched, and she said he is kind but it is not on her mind.

qa.q: What line did Ishita practise with Aditi, and why is it useful?
qa.a: The line "Thanks for being kind, but that's not on my mind" lets Aditi stay kind and clear without owing a matching feeling.

qa.q: How might the boy be affected by the chanting?
qa.a: He may feel embarrassed too, since his feelings were made public, though the note does not say how he reacted.

grounding: A child teased about a boy's crush feels embarrassed and learns a kind way to say she is not thinking about it.

passage: Arnab was cycling home from tuition when a friend told him, half laughing, that Kalyan liked the boy from the sweetshop family. Arnab kept pedalling, but his chest felt heavy, like a bag of wet sand. At home he ate little and went up to the roof. He cried for a while where nobody could see. Then he told his older cousin, who did not say much, only listened and brought him a glass of water. The next day Kalyan smiled at him at the school tap, as he always did. He smiled back a little late. He wanted to say something mean about the sweetshop boy, but he decided not to.

qa.q: Where did Arnab cry?
qa.a: He cried on the roof where nobody could see.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when he heard about Kalyan's crush, and how can you tell?
qa.a: He felt hurt and sad, since his chest felt heavy like a bag of wet sand, he ate little and he cried.

qa.q: What helped Arnab cope, and what did he choose not to do?
qa.a: He cried, talked to his cousin who listened, and stayed friendly with Kalyan; he chose not to say something mean about the other boy.

qa.q: How might Kalyan see Arnab's smile at the tap?
qa.a: Kalyan probably has no idea what he is going through, since he smiled as always, and Arnab's late smile may just seem shy to him.

grounding: A child finds out his crush likes someone else, feels the ache, talks to someone and stays kind.

passage: Nandini, you asked me if it is wrong to like someone. No, it is not. When I was eleven I liked a girl named Salma in my class, and my ears burned whenever she answered a question. I knew she might feel nothing for me, and I was fine with it. I never followed her home or sent notes through other children. I just said good morning and shared my guavas when she sat nearby. When her family moved away, I was sad for a month, but I had nothing to be sorry for. Liking somebody gives you a warm feeling to carry, beti, not a right to them. -- Farida

qa.q: How old was Farida at the time of liking Salma?
qa.a: Farida was eleven.

qa.q: How did Farida feel about the chance that Salma might not feel the same?
qa.a: Farida felt calm and at peace with it; knowing Salma might feel nothing in return, Farida was fine with that and never pushed.

qa.q: What does respecting someone's feelings look like in Farida's story?
qa.a: Farida never followed Salma home or sent notes through other children, and only said good morning and shared guavas.

qa.q: How might Salma have felt about Farida's behaviour?
qa.a: Salma was probably comfortable, since Farida never pestered her and just said good morning, though the story does not say Salma knew about the feelings.

grounding: An elder recalls a gentle crush that never pushed, followed or pestered.

passage: Thursday. At lunch Abhinav and the boys started singing "Yusuf-Zoya, Yusuf-Zoya" over and over and banging their tiffins. My face burned. Zoya looked at the floor. I felt so small and a bit angry. I said, "Stop, that isn't fun for me." Abhinav stopped first and said, "Okay, okay," and after a bit the others did too. I still felt shaky for the rest of the day. I think it hurt Zoya too. Tomorrow I will tell Abhinav that jokes about cricket are fine but not about this. -- Yusuf

qa.q: What did the boys bang while chanting?
qa.a: They banged their tiffins.

qa.q: How did Yusuf feel while the boys chanted, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Yusuf felt humiliated and a bit angry, since Yusuf's face burned and Yusuf felt small.

qa.q: What did Yusuf do that worked to stop the teasing?
qa.a: Yusuf said clearly, "Stop, that isn't fun for me," and Abhinav stopped first, then the others.

qa.q: How might Zoya have felt during the chanting?
qa.a: Zoya looked at the floor, so Zoya probably felt embarrassed too, and Yusuf thinks it hurt Zoya as well.

grounding: A child humiliated by friends' crush chanting says stop, and they do.

passage: In the packed, noisy library period, with the unit test ten minutes away, Raghavi should have been revising. Instead she watched Hemant across the table and made up a whole story: he was brilliant at cricket, kind to everyone and never angry. Then he snapped at the boy beside him for touching his pen, sulked, and knocked over his water bottle. Raghavi blinked. He was just a boy who got irritated and made a mess. Oddly, she liked that too. She did not think about changing her hair or her laugh for him. She turned back to her notes, and the daydream grew smaller while the real Hemant seemed more interesting.

qa.q: How much time was left before the unit test?
qa.a: It was ten minutes away.

qa.q: What did Raghavi think about Hemant at first, and what shook that picture?
qa.a: She imagined he was brilliant, kind and never angry, but seeing him snap over a pen and sulk showed her he had flaws.

qa.q: What does Raghavi do that shows a healthy way to hold a crush?
qa.a: She enjoys the feeling, notices the real Hemant with his flaws, and goes back to her revision instead of changing herself for him.

qa.q: How might Hemant see the moment when he snapped over the pen?
qa.a: Hemant was probably just irritated about his pen and had no idea anybody was building a perfect picture of him.

grounding: A child's idealised picture of her crush meets the real, imperfect boy, and she keeps enjoying the feeling without changing herself.

passage: I'm Madhuri, Vandana's cousin, and I was doing homework at her dining table when her mother pulled a folded note out of the laundry. Auntie read it, and her eyebrows shot up. She laughed once, then stopped. "Who is this Rohit?" Vandana went pink to her ears and grabbed for the note. "Don't read it!" Auntie took a breath, sat down, and spoke in a much softer voice. "It's natural to like someone, Vandana. We can talk about it. I won't tell anyone." Vandana said nothing, but her shoulders came down. I couldn't tell whether she felt safe or just embarrassed.

qa.q: Where did Vandana's mother find the note?
qa.a: She found it in the laundry.

qa.q: What might Vandana have been feeling when her mother read the note, and what tells you?
qa.a: She was probably embarrassed and exposed, since she went pink to her ears and grabbed for the note, though Madhuri cannot be sure.

qa.q: What did Vandana's mother do that helped after her first reaction?
qa.a: She took a breath, sat down, said it was natural to like someone and promised not to tell anyone.

qa.q: How might Vandana's mother feel on finding the note?
qa.a: She was probably surprised and unsure, since she laughed once and stopped before softening her voice.

grounding: A cousin observes a mother finding a crush note, reacting sharply, then calming and offering to talk.

passage: On the school bus, Noor mentioned that Aryan had a nice smile, and Hafsa's stomach dropped like a lift. She had liked Aryan since the start of term and had never told a soul. She stared at the traffic, said, "Oh, he's okay," and felt her cheeks go hot. For two days they walked to class with strange gaps in their talk. Finally, over a shared packet of chips at the tuck shop, Hafsa said, "I like him too. It feels weird." Noor blinked, then laughed with relief. "It IS weird! Let's not fight over this. You are more important than he is." They agreed the two of them came first, whatever Aryan did. 😅

qa.q: Where did Noor say Aryan had a nice smile?
qa.a: Noor said it on the school bus.

qa.q: How did Hafsa feel when Noor mentioned Aryan, and why did she say "Oh, he's okay"?
qa.a: Hafsa felt anxious and embarrassed, since her stomach dropped and her cheeks went hot; she liked Aryan too and was not ready to say so.

qa.q: What did Hafsa and Noor do that kept their friendship safe?
qa.a: Hafsa admitted honestly that she liked him too, and they agreed not to fight over him, since the two of them came first.

qa.q: How might Noor have felt on hearing Hafsa's confession?
qa.a: Noor blinked and then laughed with relief, so Noor probably felt relieved and glad to have it out in the open.

grounding: Two best friends like the same boy, admit the awkwardness, and put their friendship first.
